nodes.name: AI Existential Risk — What Is Real and What Is Speculative
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 12) surveying the AI existential-risk hypothesis: literary origins (Shelley, Butler, Asimov's Three Laws), I.J. Good's intelligence explosion, Bostrom's control/alignment and orthogonality theses, the three risk mechanisms, empirical signals (sleeper agents, alignment faking, reward tampering, the treacherous turn), and a considered split of what is realistic vs. speculative.
nodes.languageNotes: Static lesson; the embedded loadAiExistentialRiskModule() is a no-op placeholder returning Promise.resolve().

nodes.name: Closing the Loop — AI for Science
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 11) on AI as a discovery engine: AlphaFold/AlphaFold 3/AlphaMissense, the 2026 OpenAI Navier–Stokes singularity proof with Lean 4 formalization, AlphaTensor/FunSearch/AlphaEvolve, GNoME, weather models, and the framing that prediction and discovery become one act.
nodes.languageNotes: Static lesson with an AlphaFold pLDDT-coloured figure; loadAiForScienceModule() is a no-op placeholder.

nodes.name: Alignment — Making Objectives Match Intent
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 7) on the alignment program: the specification problem, the RLHF/RLAIF/Constitutional AI/DPO toolkit, failure modes (mesa-optimization, deceptive alignment, reward tampering), the two research programs of scalable oversight and the control problem, and interpretability as a safety instrument.
nodes.languageNotes: Static lesson; cross-links to security_inference, philosophy, and frontier chapters; loadAlignmentModule() is a no-op placeholder.

nodes.name: appendix.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Appendix lesson with four canvas/plot visualizations: Taylor-series sine approximation, the group structure of positional embeddings (clock + Cayley table), the layer-interference 'wave geometry', and probability isosurfaces ('truth tunnels'). Uses a lazy IntersectionObserver registry and re-renders on theme toggle.
nodes.languageNotes: Functions are module-scoped globals; _appLazyRegister/_appLazyCreateObserver implement on-scroll lazy init; re-renders on window.__MN_DARK theme change.

nodes.name: initTaylorSeries
nodes.summary: Builds the interactive Taylor-series sine plot: a slider for the number of polynomial terms N, a live formula display, and a canvas/plot overlaying the truncated polynomial against the true sine curve over [-2π, 2π].

nodes.name: initGroupStructureDemo
nodes.summary: Builds the group-structure interactive: sliders for elements a, b of the clock group ℤ₁₂, a compass/rotation plot, and a Cayley table showing closure, identity, and inverses of the sinusoidal positional-encoding rotation matrices.

nodes.name: initLayerWave
nodes.summary: Initializes the 'interference pattern of layers' wave-geometry visualization, computing per-layer activation waves and a dimension heatmap to explain how signal propagates and interferes through a network.

nodes.name: initIsosurface
nodes.summary: Initializes the 'isosurfaces of probability / truth tunnels' 3D visualization that renders level sets of a sentence's probability distribution and lets the user step through and inspect a sentence.

nodes.name: Appendix
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 13) serving as the book's reference appendix: grokking, symbol-convention disambiguation, sine/cosine via Taylor series, the group structure of positional embeddings, layer-interference wave geometry, and probability isosurfaces, each paired with an interactive widget.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes Markdown prose with raw-HTML interactive containers (sliders, canvases) that appendix.js initializes.

nodes.name: beyond_llms.js
nodes.summary: Placeholder module for the 'Beyond LLMs' lesson; loadBeyondLlmsModule() only updates the loading status and resolves immediately with no interactive content.

nodes.name: Beyond LLMs — The Wider World of Algorithms & Models
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 4), a wide tour of non-LLM machine learning: the Wake-Sleep/Helmholtz algorithm, clustering (k-means, hierarchical, DBSCAN, EM/GMM), classical supervised methods (trees, forests, gradient boosting, SVMs), Bayesian inference (MCMC, VI, GPs), evolutionary and RL methods, symbolic AI, recommender systems, time series, graphs, dimensionality reduction, and more, capped by an 80+ algorithm model-zoo table.
nodes.languageNotes: Long reference lesson with many math-heavy data-optionaltitle blocks and a large algorithm summary table; no embedded JS module of its own (loads the no-op beyond_llms.js).

nodes.name: Why Do Networks Generalize?
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 5) on the open theory of deep learning: why over-parameterized nets that memorize still generalize, covering double descent and benign overfitting, the loss landscape and edge of stability, NTK/NNGP lazy limits, implicit bias and neural collapse, and three partial explanatory lenses (kernel, sparsity/lottery ticket, grokking).
nodes.languageNotes: Math-heavy static lesson (math level 75); loadDeepTheoryModule() is a no-op placeholder; cross-links to frontier, optimizerlab, and coherent_difference.

nodes.name: Frontier Topics
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 6) surveying the 2025 research frontier: Constitutional AI, sparse autoencoders, long-context techniques, process reward models, Mixture-of-Depths, test-time training, agentic architectures, world models, multilingual/low-resource AI, memory and continual learning, and the mechanistic-interpretability frontier.
nodes.languageNotes: Survey lesson with several math-gated blocks; loadFrontierModule() is a no-op placeholder.

nodes.name: The Global AI Ecosystem
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 1) correcting the Silicon-Valley-centric narrative: a geography of AI across China, India, Africa, the UAE, France, Korea, Japan, Singapore, Israel, Russia, Canada, and the EU, plus open-source as a global equalizer and the geopolitics of a multipolar future.
nodes.languageNotes: Static survey lesson; loadGlobalAiEcosystemModule() is a no-op placeholder.

nodes.name: The Mind That Built Machines
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 3) on the cognitive, psychological, and evolutionary prerequisites of AI: the expensive-tissue hypothesis, the social and predictive brain, reward as RL, chunking and the working-memory bottleneck, abstraction and analogy, the psychology of the scientific mind, and the social ratchet of cumulative culture.
nodes.languageNotes: Long essay-style lesson with figures (flames, cave hands, Galileo, Poincaré, Simon & Newell) and math-gated reward/TD block; no embedded JS module.

nodes.name: AI Law & Regulation
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 8) on the legal landscape around AI: the EU AI Act risk pyramid, GDPR and data-protection cases, copyright over training data (US and EU), the US patchwork of executive orders and state laws, Chinese regulation, AI liability, sectoral rules, and international coordination.
nodes.languageNotes: Static reference lesson with a marginfig (Justitia statue); no embedded JS module.

nodes.name: Common Myths and Misconceptions About AI
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 12) reading popular AI beliefs through the folklorist Brednich's method for urban legends: is it a mind (aliveness, the Turing Test, computational theory of mind), a danger (singularity, job loss), trustworthy or unprecedented, plus the legends that turned out to be true (deepfakes, invented cases, the winning painting).
nodes.languageNotes: Static essay lesson with marginfigs (Flammarion, Turing, Cajal, Justitia); no embedded JS module.

nodes.name: philosophy.js
nodes.summary: Interactive module for the Philosophy lesson implementing three visualizations as self-contained IIFEs: an Inuktitut Chinese-Room conversation simulator (CRSim), a presheaf/sheaf 'glue' visualization (SheafViz), and a concept-direction / linear-representation steering demo (PhiloLinearRep).
nodes.languageNotes: Three top-level IIFE objects (CRSim, SheafViz, PhiloLinearRep) plus loadPhilosophyModule() which boots CRSim and PhiloLinearRep; re-renders on theme toggle.

nodes.name: CRSim
nodes.summary: Chinese-Room simulator (Inuktitut edition): slides Inuktitut inputs under a door, has the user pick the matching output from a rulebook of string-rewriting rules, then reveals the English translations to dramatize that symbol manipulation without understanding is not comprehension.

nodes.name: SheafViz
nodes.summary: Interactive visualization of sheaf theory as a metaphor for local-to-global consistency: places 'germs' at points, forms stalks, shows the presheaf, and glues compatible local data into a global sheaf on a 2D canvas.

nodes.name: PhiloLinearRep
nodes.summary: Interactive demo of linear representations and concept-direction steering: adds a steering vector to a context embedding to shift a target concept's probability while leaving causally separable concepts unchanged, based on the Park et al. (2024) intervention result.

nodes.name: Philosophical and societal implications, ethical usage of AI
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 9) on reason and intelligence: forms of logical reasoning, the Turing Test, Moravec's paradox, the Winograd schema, the Chinese Room argument, the vector grounding problem, Mary's Room, sentience, and the ethics of AI usage, with an interactive Chinese-Room simulator and a sheaf-theory visualization.
nodes.languageNotes: Long lesson hosting raw-HTML widgets wired to philosophy.js (chinese-room-sim, sheaf-canvas, philosophy-linear-rep-container).

nodes.name: software.js
nodes.summary: Placeholder module for the 'Software' lesson; loadSoftwareModule() only updates the loading status and resolves immediately with no interactive content.

nodes.name: Software: Operating Systems, Programming Languages & the Abstraction Stack
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 12) tracing the ladder of abstractions that makes AI possible: operating systems (Multics/Unix, the Altair and MS-DOS race), programming languages and compilers, libraries and frameworks, and the competing labs (Bell Labs vs MIT, Xerox PARC, the browser wars) that built the stack.
nodes.languageNotes: Long historical essay; loads the no-op software.js module.

nodes.name: Unexpected Capabilities of LLMs
nodes.summary: Part 6 lesson (order 10) cataloguing LLM capabilities that surprised researchers and were not in the training objective: in-context learning and induction heads, chain-of-thought, Othello-GPT world models, theory of mind, Toolformer, emergent translation, superposition, the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, self-improvement, verbatim memorization, and more, ending with the phase-transition pattern.
nodes.languageNotes: Long catalog essay with a math-gated in-context-statistical-learning block; no embedded JS module.

nodes.name: untold_history.js
nodes.summary: Placeholder module for the 'Untold History' lesson; loadUntoldHistoryModule() only updates the loading status and resolves immediately with no interactive content.
